title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
author: Anthropic
description: As our merges per day grew more than tenfold, source control became our biggest development bottleneck. Here, we share how we migrated to an in-house version control system in five months.
summary: Updated October 15 to include more detail on the projects that pioneered many of the techniques we use in Scion. At Anthropic, coding is no longer the bottleneck to building systems or doing research.
takeaways: Unsurprisingly, Anthropic uses Claude to write software far more than almost any other company, so we’re often the first to see where tools built for human scale start to strain.

Taking a step back, we noticed that, like most companies, we were using git as a centralized system with one authoritative copy, but nearly all of our clients were agents and jobs that are online by definition.
In May 2026, Anthropic averaged around 2,500 code changes merged per day; as of September, we merged over 30,000 per day.
